verdict.reasoning: The patient reports loss of appetite: "I'm having a loss of appetite. Yeah, I'm not eating very much."
The patient describes low energy: "I didn't really have energy" and clinician later: "you're not having the umph... you're just feeling a bit... weak."
The patient describes low mood: "I've been feeling down" and clinician clarifies about low mood/depression.

Symptoms of low appetite started after changing to a new law firm: "That must have started when I changed over to the new law firm. I would say months ago." and clarified as "Three months ago. Three and a half months ago."

Weight loss details: "Have you lost any weight?" – "I have a little bit"; "Roughly six months" – "Something like that"; "how much" – "less than a stone". Clinician restates: "About a stone? Yeah. Six months. Okay. Okay. Six kilos."
Repeated in HPI: "I'm having a loss of appetite. Yeah, I'm not eating very much."
Intermittent nausea without vomiting: "I feel nauseous. Every now and again" and later "You mentioned nausea. Have you been ever sick with it?" – "No, actually not."
No change in bowel habit: "How are your bowels?" – "That's okay. I would say I don't really have problems when going to the toilet." Clinician later: "you've mentioned now your bowels are fine".
Denies diarrhea: "you don't have any diarrhea?" – "No, no diarrhea? No."
No blood or mucus: "there's no blood in the poo? No mucus, nothing of that sort?" – patient does not contradict, responding "No, no, just."

Shortness of breath and palpitations in lifts: patient – "Feel like I'm feeling short of breath"; "my heart starts beating and I can't really breathe"; clinician: "You're... describing like, palpitations" – patient agrees "Yeah." Occurs "very significantly in the lift."
Denies chest pain: clinician asks "Do you get any chest pains with it?" – "Not really, no"; and later both confirm "No chest pain."

Walking tolerance and recent reduced activity: clinician asks if he feels SOB when walking – patient: "No, actually, no" and agrees to "you can walk about a mile... and you don't feel short of breath"; later he adds "I haven't been walking lately at all... it's really hard for me to identify when I feel the shortness of breath... I haven't been feeling good enough."
History of hypothyroidism: "I had too little activity of my thyroid"; clinician: "Oh, yeah. Underactive thyroid? Yes."

Previously on thyroxine, now stopped: "And in that I took thyroxine." Clinician: "You're taking thyroxine. Are you using it every day?" – patient: "Not anymore... I have not been taking it in the last... since I changed law firm."
Family history is not mentioned anywhere in the transcript, so stating it is not documented is consistent with the record.
Occupation: "Who likes to be a lawyer?" and earlier his email domain "awyers.co.uk" supports that he works as a lawyer.
Marital status: patient refers to "My wife was starting to complain as well in nightly activities." This implies he is married.

Low mood, low energy, decreased appetite for months with modest weight loss: patient "been feeling down" with little energy, "having a loss of appetite," onset "months ago" around law-firm change and weight loss "less than a stone" over ~6 months.
Episodic palpitations/SOB in lifts without chest pain: patient describes SOB with "my heart starts beating" in lifts; clinician labels as palpitations; patient denies chest pain: "No chest pain."

Hypothyroidism previously treated and currently off thyroxine: as per PMH and meds above. Clinician also explores that symptoms might coincide with stopping: "So all these things are since you've stopped taking the thyroxine." Patient: "That might be coinciding. I'm not sure."
Intermittent nausea: "I feel nauseous. Every now and again."

Unintentional weight loss of ~6 kg over about 6 months: patient reports weight loss "a little bit" over roughly six months; clinician rephrases "About a stone? Yeah. Six months. Okay. Okay. Six kilos."

The clinician says "a general set of bloods where we look at things like anemia, how your kidney functions are, your livers, all that with vitamin levels" but does not specify FBC, U&E, LFTs, TSH, FT4, iron studies, B12, folate, or vitamin D by name.
Process for arranging blood tests: "you need to ring up support and I'll do the form for you... so that we can organize that blood test for you."
Follow-up via text prompt: "once you get the result, you will receive a text message through your phone to tell you to book an appointment."
Plan for physical examination if labs normal: "If that's all clear, then we would need to do a physical examination."

Safety advice: "with palpitations or chest pain... you need to go to A and E" and "if your... bowels change or you're being sick again, you need to get in touch with us" and "If you're feeling poorly, don't wait for that. Just get in touch with us again."
Text prompt for follow-up: "you will receive a text message through your phone to tell you to book an appointment."
Advised to contact service if worse before follow-up: "If you're feeling poorly, don't wait for that. Just get in touch with us again."
